column8: Wed 18 Nov: 3c source line, the court's definition (not repaid even if royalties never exceed it), re-read at source today; only the first half of row 35's contrast; a floor per signed contract, never 'her career gives her a floor' (her next advance is pencil; repaid on non-delivery, Q95-022).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2), one source line beside Q96-012: the court's four triggers and the shift from thirds to quarters, re-read at source today; adult trade, so for her genre Q12b-016's thirds on the art stay closer.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, the evidence row 35 needs: the court's 'most' with its record's spread (Hachette about half, one agency 20%, Wylie 5%, Hill's 85% for top-selling contracts), all re-read at source today in n.4; supersedes Q96-013 as the source for most; witnesses' estimates, never a census.
Wed 18 Nov: wording guard for 2.3 and 3c: never print 70% or 7 in 10 for books that do not earn out; say most, with the court as source; the working paper's 30% stays untraced.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 3 and Q96-013 (for most books the advance is the whole pay); these are the government's words as a party, so the court's most (row 3) carries it.

Wed 18 Nov: guard on row 35, store only: Australian members' self-reports (60% earned out, mostly advances under $5,000) run the other way, so her trade's usual outcome depends on advance size; the bigger-floor-rarer-top line is Keel inference across two samples, never a finding.

Wed 18 Nov: store only: the court's 2% of acquisitions and 70% of advance money for advances of $250,000 or more; Laura's advances are not in the case, so it places no figure on her; a second 70% beside the killed one (row 4) invites confusion.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 or 3a scale, one clause at most: a $250,000 advance nets about $53,000-$71,000 a year over three to four years (Keel check holds); never implies her income or advance size (not in the case); the case already pays the ten from the portfolio, so it illustrates that choice, never argues it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c-3d word line, owed against owned (Q72, Q83): the US government's lawyers called an advance a guarantee of payment (proposed findings, a party's words, never the court's); in the report guaranteed takes the Treasuries or the stated range after the move, never a fund's payout or a dollar figure (CONCEIT V2.1).

Wed 18 Nov: store only: publishers profit at about 70% of earn-out (re-read at source today); the parallel to Laura's margin breaks on its own disanalogy (the payer's profit against the figure co-sponsors count), and a third 70% on the card confuses.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: an agent's worked example on assumed costs (text mostly from 2011); no part needs it.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c or 2.3, one clause: a publisher can promise floors because it holds thousands of books (portfolio business; only 35 out of 100 turn a profit; re-read at source today, the scan reads 3 5 and tum); Laura has one plan and ten dates, so she owns her floor instead of promising it: IPS l.11 from inside her trade, beside AHA row 2.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 12 (the payer carries unearned floors on its backlist); the court's loss and the Norton editor's overpay re-read at source today, a second source line there; Q96-010 is the government's version.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c, as row 35's bid-up clause only: keep the court's 'books generally are sold to the highest bidder'; drop the working paper's untraced 93% and the Keel 93% beside it (two 93s confuse); auctions are a minority of the biggest deals (the court: 40% of advances over $250,000, Hill), so never 'an advance is set at the second bidder's estimate' as a rule.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 14 (advances bid above realistic sales, at the payer's risk), the UK society's version; its $115,000 is today's central top, said as about $115,000 on today's figures.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: where an advance sits depends on the market (a token for educational writers, the publisher's estimate in trade); it qualifies row 14 and serves no part alone.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, at most a clause beside Q25-001 and H7-063: her trade also charges a missed top to the next deal (ASA guidance, no data); the case's own line (l.114) carries the point, so this is colour, never evidence, and nothing is attributed to Laura.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Scholastic reserves most of its unearned advances; the 59% is Keel arithmetic conditional on the net line (current portion unchecked), never quoted until checked.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: a publisher's dated commitments to creators ($37.6m, the sum checks) are someone else's promise; the contrast with Laura's ten is already carried by owned, not owed (Q72-016).

Wed 18 Nov: 3c fact at most, never a staged reserve image (publishing, not pencil and ink; reserve collides with the operating reserve, CONCEIT row 9); only the Guild's reason is new (overpayments are hard to recover), since Q12-009 has the 35% and the returns rate; the 0.5% margin's job is fund costs beyond the fee (NUMBERS 0), and the asymmetry (case l.114, Q43-031) is why any margin exists.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q12-009 (a returns reserve delays earned royalties, so less reaches January 2028); the UK limits (25%, repaid within 12 months) are a second source line there.

Wed 18 Nov: guard on CONCEIT 3a's reserve-against-returns line, whose same-shape claim needs it: a publisher's reserve holds back the receiver's money to protect the payer, while the extra Treasuries ($36,774, NUMBERS headline) are Laura's own money held so the residency is paid; with round 7 (second trade images fail blind), one more reason the reserve stays a fact, not a turn; about $46,600 matches NUMBERS ($46,566).
Wed 18 Nov: store only: rights income a publisher holds pays down an unearned advance first; which rights her publishers hold is not in the case, so never a claim about the 2028 deposit.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q96-012 (an advance takes three to four years to be paid) and Q12-033; one UK deal's calendar; that money reaching her by January 2028 comes from deals struck years before is Keel inference.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 26 (licensing's floor-and-top build: minimum guarantee, recoup, overages); vendor and legal-guide explainers.

Wed 18 Nov: store, a 3c clause at most beside row 35: in licensing the floor is set at about half the forecast on purpose (an agency's rule of thumb); Laura's bottom is not set from a forecast but counted from bonds she owns ($95,000 stated against $97,605 and a $102,365 payout, NUMBERS 4); never a second image.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of H7-070 and Q72-016 (a promised floor is only as good as its payer: owed, not owned); one firm's licence terms, no failure data.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a, a plain clause at most: licensing law asks for a minimum when the licensor has fixed costs such as facility and personnel (Contreras, read in extract); strikingly dissimilar parallel is the conceit's phrase, and as a turn this would be a second image outside pencil and ink (round 7), so say it as a fact with its disanalogy (the residency is paid by her ten payments, not royalties) and the plan's answer, ownership.

Wed 18 Nov: 3a, adapt: each payment has its own rung (IPS l.13), but the extra Treasuries are one pooled backstop whose money carries forward from earlier years to later ones (NUMBERS 8a: $6,865 after 2033 with the fee), so never 'an assured payment is not paid out of another year's surplus'; the clash it guards (later bonds' interest paying earlier payments) holds.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 12 (the payer of floors pools risk across many authors); Towse is the academic source line for it.
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Caves's mechanism (the publisher keeps every extra dollar until the advance is recouped) beside Q1-026; owed against owned is already carried by Q72-016 and row 9.

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2), a clause at most: after the last big merger advances fell for authors with a bestseller (job market paper, not peer-reviewed, read in extract); a cause outside the business cycle for a smaller 2028 deposit, never in place of IPS l.9's recession.
Wed 18 Nov: guard only, for 2.3 and row 35: no data splits earn-out by genre, so never say most of her books stop at the floor; the children's and YA claim is 2009 hearsay and is never quoted.

Wed 18 Nov: 3d, one clause: an earn-out often converts today's disagreement over price into tomorrow's litigation over the outcome (Airborne, Del. Ch. 2009, re-read at source today); why Laura names a figure only after the move has bought it; the 11 of 100 is NUMBERS 4's 10.6%, worded as the move would buy less than a top stated a year early.

Wed 18 Nov: 3c candidate clause, read cold before it takes a slot (3c holds aha rows 1 and 7): her trade's range stops at the floor for most books (row 3), hers lands on the top; NUMBERS 4 checked: the contribution 'Equals the stated top in every path' (house) and 'in every window' (history), both ends owned in every joint window; the fact is in the store (Q113-040), the reversal is new; certain takes the stated range, never $115,000.

Wed 18 Nov: 3b-3c wording guard: never map the stated top to royalties; the open-ended part is her flexibility (half kept about $21,200 plus anything above the top about $7,500; NUMBERS 4: $21,179 and $7,503), never stated and hers.

Wed 18 Nov: conceit fit test settled, consistent with round 7 and H8-046: advance and earn-out are never a turn (a second trade image, and owed pulls ink toward signed); her next advance stays only as a pencil example at the definition; money already paid is never called ink.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3, adapt: a signed contract carries a floor the publisher owes, paid in parts over years, while her next advance is pencil, so never 'her career already gives her a floor'; one clause at most, never a second mapping of her career beside IPS l.3's giant stock (CANON A1, Q96-042's note).
